title_en: Export Control Law of the People's Republic of China

articles.content_en: Article 1 This Law is enacted for the purposes of safeguarding national security and interests, fulfilling international obligations such as non-proliferation, and strengthening and regulating export controls.

Article 2 This Law shall apply to the export controls of the People's Republic of China on dual-use items, military products, nuclear items, and other goods, technologies, services, and other items related to safeguarding national security and interests and fulfilling international obligations such as non-proliferation (hereinafter collectively referred to as controlled items).
The controlled items referred to in the preceding paragraph include data such as technical materials related to the items.
For the purposes of this Law, "export controls" means the adoption of prohibitive or restrictive measures by the State on the transfer of controlled items from the territory of the People's Republic of China to outside the territory, and on the provision of controlled items by citizens, legal persons, and unincorporated organizations of the People's Republic of China to foreign organizations and individuals.
For the purposes of this Law, "dual-use items" means goods, technologies, and services that have both civil and military uses or that help enhance military potential, in particular those that may be used for the design, development, production, or use of weapons of mass destruction and their means of delivery.
For the purposes of this Law, "military products" means equipment, specialized production equipment, and other related goods, technologies, and services used for military purposes.
For the purposes of this Law, "nuclear items" means nuclear materials, nuclear equipment, non-nuclear materials for reactors, and related technologies and services.

Article 3 The work on export controls shall adhere to a holistic approach to national security, uphold international peace, balance security and development, and improve export control management and services.

Article 4 The State shall implement a unified system of export controls, managed by formulating control lists, rosters, or catalogues (hereinafter collectively referred to as control lists) and implementing export licensing and other means.

Article 5 The departments of the State Council and the Central Military Commission that assume export control functions (hereinafter collectively referred to as the State export control authorities) shall be responsible for export control work according to their respective functions and duties. Other relevant departments of the State Council and the Central Military Commission shall be responsible for work related to export controls according to their respective functions and duties.
The State shall establish a coordination mechanism for export control work to coordinate and harmonize major matters concerning export controls. The State export control authorities and the relevant departments of the State Council shall closely cooperate and strengthen information sharing.
The State export control authorities shall, together with relevant departments, establish an expert consultation mechanism for export controls to provide advisory opinions on export control work.
The State export control authorities shall, when appropriate, issue export control guidelines for relevant industries to guide export operators in establishing and improving internal compliance systems for export controls and regulating their operations.
The relevant departments of the people's governments of provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government shall be responsible for work related to export controls in accordance with the provisions of laws and administrative regulations.
Article 6 The State shall strengthen international cooperation on export controls and participate in the formulation of international rules relating to export controls.

Article 7 Export operators may, according to law, establish and join relevant chambers of commerce, associations, and other industry self-regulatory organizations.
Relevant chambers of commerce, associations, and other industry self-regulatory organizations shall comply with laws and administrative regulations, provide their members with services related to export controls in accordance with their articles of association, and play a coordinating and self-regulatory role.

Article 29 When the State export control authorities perform their duties according to law, the relevant departments of the State Council, local people's governments, and their relevant departments shall provide assistance.
Where the State export control authorities, alone or jointly with relevant departments, conduct supervision, inspection, and investigation according to law, the relevant organizations and individuals shall cooperate and shall not refuse or obstruct such activities.
The relevant State organs and their staff members shall, according to law, have the obligation to keep confidential any State secrets, trade secrets, personal privacy, and personal information learned during the investigation.

Article 30 For the purpose of strengthening the management of export of controlled items and preventing the risk of illegal export of controlled items, the State export control authorities may take measures such as regulatory talks and issuing warning letters.

Article 31 Any organization or individual shall have the right to report to the State export control authorities any act suspected of violating the provisions of this Law. Upon receiving a report, the State export control authorities shall handle it in a timely manner according to law and shall keep the whistleblower confidential.

Article 32 The State export control authorities shall, in accordance with international treaties concluded or acceded to or on the principle of equality and mutual benefit, carry out export control cooperation and exchanges with other countries or regions, international organizations, etc.
Organizations and individuals within the territory of the People's Republic of China that provide information related to export controls to overseas parties shall do so according to law; if such provision may endanger national security and interests, it shall not be provided.

Article 33 Where an export operator, without having obtained the export operation qualification for relevant controlled items, engages in the export of such controlled items, a warning shall be given, the illegal act shall be ordered to cease, the illegal gains shall be confiscated, and if the illegal turnover is 500,000 RMB or more, a fine of not less than five times but not more than ten times the illegal turnover shall also be imposed; if there is no illegal turnover or the illegal turnover is less than 500,000 RMB, a fine of not less than 500,000 RMB but not more than 5,000,000 RMB shall also be imposed.

Article 35 Where a person obtains an export license for controlled items by fraudulent, bribery, or other illegitimate means, or illegally transfers an export license for controlled items, the license shall be revoked, the export license shall be confiscated, the illegal gains shall be confiscated, and if the illegal turnover is 200,000 RMB or more, a fine of not less than five times but not more than ten times the illegal turnover shall also be imposed; if there is no illegal turnover or the illegal turnover is less than 200,000 RMB, a fine of not less than 200,000 RMB but not more than 2,000,000 RMB shall also be imposed.
Where a person forges, alters, or sells an export license for controlled items, the illegal gains shall be confiscated, and if the illegal turnover is 50,000 RMB or more, a fine of not less than five times but not more than ten times the illegal turnover shall also be imposed; if there is no illegal turnover or the illegal turnover is less than 50,000 RMB, a fine of not less than 50,000 RMB but not more than 500,000 RMB shall also be imposed.

Article 36 Where a person, knowing that an export operator is engaged in illegal acts relating to export controls, still provides it with services such as agency, freight, courier, customs declaration, third-party e-commerce trading platform, and finance, a warning shall be given, the illegal act shall be ordered to cease, the illegal gains shall be confiscated, and if the illegal turnover is 100,000 RMB or more, a fine of not less than three times but not more than five times the illegal turnover shall also be imposed; if there is no illegal turnover or the illegal turnover is less than 100,000 RMB, a fine of not less than 100,000 RMB but not more than 500,000 RMB shall also be imposed.

Article 37 Where an export operator, in violation of the provisions of this Law, conducts transactions with an importer or end-user on the control list, a warning shall be given, the illegal act shall be ordered to cease, the illegal gains shall be confiscated, and if the illegal turnover is 500,000 RMB or more, a fine of not less than ten times but not more than twenty times the illegal turnover shall also be imposed; if there is no illegal turnover or the illegal turnover is less than 500,000 RMB, a fine of not less than 500,000 RMB but not more than 5,000,000 RMB shall also be imposed; if the circumstances are serious, the operator shall be ordered to suspend business for rectification, until the relevant export operation qualification for controlled items is revoked.

Article 38 Where an export operator refuses or obstructs supervision and inspection, a warning shall be given, and a fine of not less than 100,000 RMB but not more than 300,000 RMB shall also be imposed; if the circumstances are serious, the operator shall be ordered to suspend business for rectification, until the relevant export operation qualification for controlled items is revoked.

Article 39 Where an export operator has been penalized for violating the provisions of this Law, the State export control authorities may, from the date on which the penalty decision takes effect, refuse to accept its application for an export license within five years; with respect to the directly responsible person in charge and other directly liable persons, they may be prohibited from engaging in relevant export business activities within five years, and if they have received criminal punishment for an illegal act relating to export controls, they shall be prohibited from engaging in relevant export business activities for life.
The State export control authorities shall, according to law, include the export operator's violation of this Law in the credit record.

Article 40 Export control illegal acts as provided for in this Law shall be penalized by the State export control authorities; where laws and administrative regulations provide that the customs shall impose penalties, the customs shall impose penalties in accordance with this Law.

Article 41 Where an interested organization or individual disagrees with the decision of the national export control authority to deny a license, it or he may apply for administrative reconsideration according to law. The decision on administrative reconsideration shall be a final ruling.
Article 42 Any national staff member engaged in export control management who neglects duty, engages in malpractices for personal gain, or abuses authority shall be given a sanction according to law.

Article 43 Any violation of the provisions of this Law on export control management that endangers national security and interests shall, in addition to being subject to penalties in accordance with this Law, also be subject to handling and penalties in accordance with the provisions of relevant laws and administrative regulations.
Any violation of this Law by exporting controlled items that the State prohibits from export or by exporting controlled items without a license shall be subject to criminal liability according to law.

Article 44 Any organization or individual outside the territory of the People's Republic of China that violates the provisions of this Law on export control management, endangers the national security and interests of the People's Republic of China, or hinders the fulfillment of international obligations such as non-proliferation shall be dealt with according to law and its or his legal liability shall be investigated.

Article 45 The transit, transshipment, through shipment, re-export of controlled items, or export from special customs supervision zones such as bonded zones and export processing zones and from bonded supervision places such as export supervised warehouses and bonded logistics centers to outside the territory shall be carried out in accordance with the relevant provisions of this Law.
Article 46 Where this Law does not provide for the export of nuclear and other controlled items, the provisions of relevant laws and administrative regulations shall apply.

Article 47 The export of military products for the overseas deployment of armed forces, foreign military exchanges, military assistance, etc., shall be carried out in accordance with the provisions of relevant laws and regulations.

Article 48 Where any country or region abuses export control measures to endanger the national security and interests of the People's Republic of China, the People's Republic of China may take reciprocal measures against such country or region based on the actual circumstances.
Article 49 This Law shall come into force as of December 1, 2020.
